picture.alt: A night market after dark: red paper lanterns and lit stalls behind, a crowd and city buildings in the distance. Four young friends lean over a stall counter around a big metal tray of fried stinky tofu (golden tofu cubes with brown sauce, chopped green onion and pickled cabbage), with steam rising from it. From left: a girl with short wavy brown hair and round glasses, a white shirt under a dark-purple vest and a backpack, smiles with her mouth open and holds the tray out toward the others; a boy with black hair, in an open light-green shirt over a red striped T-shirt, leans back with both hands raised, palms out, looking worried; a boy with short spiky black hair, in a dark-blue jacket over a red T-shirt, rests one hand on his chin and smiles as he leans toward the tofu; a girl with long wavy dark hair and hoop earrings, in a bright-blue denim jacket over an orange top and white trousers, smiles and looks at the tofu. Nobody is eating.

passage.traditional: 我剛來台灣的時候，不太{1}吃台灣菜，也不敢吃臭豆腐。後來，我的台灣室友常常帶我去夜市，還{2}我吃各種小吃，所以我{3}喜歡台灣小吃了，現在臭豆腐我也敢吃了。週末的時候，我們也常常一起去{4}，買了很多又好看又便宜的衣服，花的錢也不多。

passage.pinyin: Wǒ gāng lái Táiwān de shíhòu, bú tài xíguàn chī Táiwān cài, yě bù gǎn chī chòu dòufǔ. Hòulái, wǒ de Táiwān shìyǒu chángcháng dài wǒ qù yèshì, hái tuījiàn wǒ chī gè zhǒng xiǎochī, suǒyǐ wǒ yuè lái yuè xǐhuān Táiwān xiǎochī le, xiànzài chòu dòufǔ wǒ yě gǎn chī le. Zhōumò de shíhòu, wǒmen yě chángcháng yìqǐ qù guàngjiē, mǎi le hěn duō yòu hǎokàn yòu piányí de yīfu, huā de qián yě bù duō.

Later my Taiwanese roommate often took me to night markets and recommended all kinds of snacks to me, so I came to like Taiwanese snacks more and more; now I even dare to eat stinky tofu. At weekends we often went shopping together too, and bought lots of clothes that look good and are cheap without spending much.

questions.why: 不太習慣吃台灣菜: at first the food felt unfamiliar; the later sentences show how that changed.
推薦我吃各種小吃: the roommate recommended snacks for the writer to try (推薦 + person + 吃).
越來越喜歡……了: after many night-market trips the writer likes the snacks more and more; 越來越 goes before the verb.
一起去逛街: they went shopping together and came back with clothes.

passage.traditional: 上個星期六晚上，我跟室友去逛夜市。週末的夜市{1}得不得了，買一個雞排要排隊排二十分鐘。我們一邊逛，一邊吃了臭豆腐、蚵仔煎和豆花，最後兩個人都吃{2}了。要回家的時候，{3}下了很大的雨，我們在一家飲料店等了半個小時才回家。雖然回家很晚，可是我們都覺得這個晚上過得很{4}。
passage.simplified: 上个星期六晚上，我跟室友去逛夜市。周末的夜市{1}得不得了，买一个鸡排要排队排二十分钟。我们一边逛，一边吃了臭豆腐、蚵仔煎和豆花，最后两个人都吃{2}了。要回家的时候，{3}下了很大的雨，我们在一家饮料店等了半个小时才回家。虽然回家很晚，可是我们都觉得这个晚上过得很{4}。

Wǒmen yìbiān guàng, yìbiān chī le chòu dòufǔ, ézǐjiān hé dòuhuā, zuìhòu liǎng ge rén dōu chībǎo le. Yào huí jiā de shíhòu, hūrán xià le hěn dà de yǔ, wǒmen zài yì jiā yǐnliào diàn děng le bàn ge xiǎoshí cái huí jiā. Suīrán huí jiā hěn wǎn, kěshì wǒmen dōu juéde zhège wǎnshàng guò de hěn yúkuài.

As we strolled we ate stinky tofu, oyster omelet and tofu pudding, and in the end we were both full. 忽然下了很大的雨: the rain came suddenly, just as they were leaving.
過得很愉快: 雖然……可是 turns it around: they got home late, but the evening was pleasant.

My roommate isn't interested in food. She likes buying clothes, and she's great at haggling: she often gets a hundred dollars off a piece of clothing.

text.traditional: 我跟姐姐下個月要搬家了。新的公寓離學校很近，走路五分鐘就到了。房間不大，可是看起來很乾淨。房東人很好，除了替我們裝了網路，還送給我們兩張書桌。房租一個月一萬，不包括水費和電費，可是我們都很滿意。
text.simplified: 我跟姐姐下个月要搬家了。新的公寓离学校很近，走路五分钟就到了。房间不大，可是看起来很干净。房东人很好，除了替我们装了网路，还送给我们两张书桌。房租一个月一万，不包括水费和电费，可是我们都很满意。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn jiějie xià ge yuè yào bānjiā le. Xīn de gōngyù lí xuéxiào hěn jìn, zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le. Fángjiān bú dà, kěshì kànqǐlái hěn gānjìng. text.english: My older sister and I are moving next month. The new apartment is close to school, a five-minute walk. The rooms aren't big, but they look clean. The landlord is very nice: besides setting up the internet for us, he also gave us two desks. The rent is ten thousand a month, not including water and electricity, but we're both very happy with it.

text.traditional: 上個星期六中午，我請朋友來我家吃飯。我本來想星期四晚上打掃房間，可是那天我在圖書館念書，念到十點才回家。星期五晚上我又得去餐廳幫忙，所以星期六早上我七點就起來了，先把地掃了，再把桌子擦一擦。朋友到的時候，房間已經很乾淨了。
text.simplified: 上个星期六中午，我请朋友来我家吃饭。我本来想星期四晚上打扫房间，可是那天我在图书馆念书，念到十点才回家。星期五晚上我又得去餐厅帮忙，所以星期六早上我七点就起来了，先把地扫了，再把桌子擦一擦。朋友到的时候，房间已经很干净了。
text.pinyin: Shàng ge xīngqíliù zhōngwǔ, wǒ qǐng péngyǒu lái wǒ jiā chīfàn. Wǒ běnlái xiǎng xīngqísì wǎnshàng dǎsǎo fángjiān, kěshì nà tiān wǒ zài túshūguǎn niànshū, niàn dào shí diǎn cái huí jiā. Xīngqíwǔ wǎnshàng wǒ yòu děi qù cāntīng bāngmáng, suǒyǐ xīngqíliù zǎoshàng wǒ qī diǎn jiù qǐlái le, xiān bǎ dì sǎo le, zài bǎ zhuōzi cā yì cā. Péngyǒu dào de shíhòu, fángjiān yǐjīng hěn gānjìng le.
text.english: Last Saturday at noon I had friends over for lunch. I'd meant to clean my room on Thursday evening, but that day I studied at the library and didn't get home until ten. On Friday evening I had to help at the restaurant, so on Saturday I got up at seven, swept the floor and then gave the table a wipe. By the time my friends arrived, the room was already clean.

prompt.traditional: 這個人是什麼時候打掃房間的？
prompt.simplified: 这个人是什么时候打扫房间的？
prompt.pinyin: Zhège rén shì shénme shíhòu dǎsǎo fángjiān de?
prompt.english: When did the writer clean the room?

questions.why: 星期四……十點才回家 and 星期五……又得去餐廳幫忙, so the cleaning happened 星期六早上. Thursday was only the plan, and by noon on Saturday the room was already clean.
